text:
For the choirmaster: on the sheminith.[^1] A psalm of David.

[^1]: A musical term of uncertain meaning; possibly an eight-stringed instrument or a lower octave.

versions.text: For the choirmaster: on the sheminith. A psalm of David.
versions.explanation: The transliterated term "sheminith" will be opaque to listeners and readers. A brief footnote clarifies that it is an uncertain musical direction without cluttering the read-aloud text.

text: Help, LORD, for the faithful are gone; the loyal have vanished from among the children of men.
Everyone lies to his neighbor; they speak with flattering lips and a double heart.
May the LORD cut off all flattering lips, every tongue that boasts of great things—
those who say, "With our tongues we will prevail; our lips are our own—who is master over us?"
"Because the poor are plundered and the needy groan, now I will arise," says the LORD. "I will set them in the safety they long for."

versions.text: "Because the poor are plundered and the needy groan, now I will arise," says the LORD. "I will place them in the safety for which they long."
versions.explanation: The clause "in the safety for which they long" is stiff for oral reading; the relative construction breaks the rhythm of the divine oracle. "I will set them in the safety they long for" is smoother and equally faithful to the difficult Hebrew (אָשִׁית בְּיֵשַׁע יָפִיחַ לוֹ).

text: The words of the LORD are pure words, silver refined in a furnace of earth, purified seven times over.
You, O LORD, will keep them; you will guard us from this generation forever.
The wicked prowl on every side when vileness is exalted among the children of men.
